name: Letter of intent
what: A short letter that proposes the main deal terms before a contract is drafted, usually non-binding except for named provisions.

fields.label: Buyer
fields.definition: The proposed buyer, often an entity to be formed.

fields.label: Property
fields.definition: Address and a short description of what is being bought.

fields.label: Earnest money
fields.definition: The deposit and when it goes hard.

fields.label: Feasibility period
fields.definition: Days the buyer has to investigate and terminate.

fields.label: Closing
fields.definition: Days from the effective date, or from the end of feasibility, to closing.

fields.label: Financing
fields.definition: Whether closing depends on a loan, and on what terms.

fields.label: Title and survey
fields.definition: Who orders and pays for the title policy and survey.

fields.label: Binding provisions
fields.definition: The provisions meant to bind the parties, such as confidentiality or exclusivity.

fields.label: Offer expires
fields.definition: The date the proposal lapses if not accepted.
